protocol.transformDescription: Each whole source scene shrinks onto a 1920 by 1080 RGB127 gray canvas at a fixed, hash-derived position. Sixteen-times fractional coverage is integrated to the saved pixels. The scene is never re-enlarged to native size. Original inputs retain their native dimensions. Both methods receive the identical saved bytes; tiled scanning adds four overlapping tiles to the shared whole-frame context pass.
protocol.notes: Development stress test, not independent field accuracy or calibrated drone range. The illustrative 10/20/50/100 m labels assume a 5 cm target and a 1380 px focal length; actual organism sizes, camera intrinsics and distances were not measured. A selected region can be a cluster. The previous round-4 downsample-then-restore information-loss test is different and must not be merged with this curve. Two concurrent CPU workers used four Torch threads each; method timings include contention and cannot be compared directly with earlier sequential CPU timings. Tiled timing includes the shared raw pass, so adding raw and tiled time double-counts it. All five negative controls are native-only, separated by human versus AI authority. Extra selected-region overlaps are counted as unmatched alerts; no accuracy conclusion is assigned to unmarked regions in incomplete photographs. An independent read-only audit found broad detector alerts in tiles containing only uniform RGB127 padding. Synthetic extra-box totals therefore include padding artifacts and are not field false-positive rates; no alert was removed or rescored after observing this behavior.
limitations: Previously inspected reference regions are a development regression, not independent field accuracy.
Three human targets share one video; nine AI photo targets remain approximate and incomplete, including clusters as well as individual bodies.
All synthetic views shrink the whole source onto a fixed 1920x1080 RGB127 canvas with 16x coverage integration. They are never re-enlarged to native footprint.
Gray borders, scene edges, fixed placement, resampling and model resizing differ from real camera motion; no new optical detail is created.
Placement is SHA-derived before inference; focal positions are clamped only to keep the entire scene inside the canvas. Actual tile coverage is recorded.
Fractional widths and heights describe projected annotation geometry, not guaranteed recoverable fungal texture. A subpixel width may have a height above one pixel.
10/20/50/100 metres are illustrative only: widthPixels = 1380px * 0.05m / distance. The sources have no measured lens, organism width or range.
The old round-4 downsample-then-re-enlarge test is a separate information-loss experiment and is not the small-footprint curve reported here.
Each region can match at most one prediction. Extra overlaps and other unmatched boxes are reported; incomplete AI positives cannot establish false-positive rates.
Five negative controls are native-only: one saved human absence and four earlier AI absence opinions. They establish no distance-dependent false-positive rate.
Two isolated CPU workers use four Torch threads each. Tiled timing includes its shared raw context pass; method times must not be added as elapsed runtime.
Concurrent-worker latency includes CPU contention and is not directly comparable to earlier sequential-worker timing.
No training, score tuning, active-model changes, source-label changes or aircraft commands occur.

recovery.notes: Original failed report and92saved predictions are preserved unchanged. Only9missing frozen jobs are rerun. The failed executor may have completed unrecorded in-flight work, so total attempted forwards are unknown.505means unique persisted planned forwards, not a clean uninterrupted505forward run. Elapsed wall time includes the interruption and recovery.

protocol.verificationScope: Independent consistency and localization recount from saved predictions and frozen pixels; not independent human confirmation or proof of field accuracy.
